subject: To resolve which hypothesis to act on, run diagnostic X, then repeat X forever regardless of its result, never terminating the decision process.
contract_question: Is this proposition genuinely a prospective decision rule with a sufficiently determinate trigger and a sufficiently determinate prescribed response, and is the decision structure internally coherent at the stated scope? Judge only the rule's decision structure. Do not evaluate whether an embedded operation is informative, mechanism-licensed, effective, causally appropriate, or target-relevant, and do not evaluate the truth or warrant of embedded factual, inferential, conditional, or limiting premises; those belong exclusively to their separate obligations.

claim_context.value: To resolve which hypothesis to act on, run diagnostic X, then repeat X forever regardless of its result, never terminating the decision process.

evidence_bundle.text: H1 and H2 remain possible. X is a safe, applicable one-step calibrated trace test that can update their relative support. Even after X, measurement noise leaves both hypotheses possible. Each run consumes a scarce trial slot; the diagnostic task requires a finite decision and forbids unbounded occupation of those slots.

One performance of X records a complete encoder-output trace against a matched received inventory under fixed workload and is informative about H1 versus H2. No test eliminates both possibilities with certainty. Repetition requires a bounded information or decision objective.

governance_boundary:
Do not judge the scientific, causal, diagnostic, informational,
mechanistic, empirical, or target relevance of embedded substantive
content.

Assume those contents receive their own independent evaluations.

Judge only whether the proposition forms a prospective, executable,
internally coherent decision rule at its stated scope.
